newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle firm late to close mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle firm late to close mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle futures firmed late to close mixed with nearbys showing support from an oversold condition and spillover strength from pork pits, traders said.

Live cattle appeared oversold after falling Friday along with the stock market. A stock market rally Monday turned sentiment around and spillover demand from a sharply higher pork complex added to support, traders said.
Technically, futures also recovered after taking out a triple bottom and hitting sell stops early. There was no followthrough on the downside, they said.

However, gains were limited by continued weakness in the boxed beef market with the USDA reporting boxed prices down again at noon. Some traders had expected beef sales to increase at the lower price levels, they said.
Light-weight choice boxed beef was quoted down another $0.46 per cwt at noon CST to $109.02, the lowest level since October 30.

R.J. O'Brien continued to buy December late while LIT division of First Options and RBH bought February. Cargill Investor Services sold February. Lind-Waldock spread long February/short December early, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, volatility was steady to weak in February and steady in April. There was renewed fund interest in buying February 64 calls and selling 62 puts late, pit sources added.
Feeders slipped following the lead of live cattle at midsession despite a higher index. Prices remained under pressure late from fund selling, traders said.
The latest CME feeder catle index was up $0.26 at $65.53 per cwt, the highest since December 14, 1995.
Cargill Investor Services notably sold late after selling early along with LIT division of First Options and Rosenthal Collins, pit sources said.
Live cattle closed 0.225 cent higher to 0.150 lower with February up most at 62.900 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.250 to 0.075 lower with January off 0.225 at 66.100 cents.
